input.sql:
WITH gauge AS (
  SELECT obs_date, mm
  FROM pluvia.ghcn_prcp
  WHERE station_id = 'NIM00065201'
    AND obs_date BETWEEN '2025-07-01' AND '2025-07-31'
),
sat AS (
  SELECT obs_date, mm
  FROM pluvia.power_lagos_2025_daily
  WHERE latitude = 6.577 AND longitude = 3.321
    AND obs_date BETWEEN '2025-07-01' AND '2025-07-31'
),
overlap AS (
  SELECT g.obs_date, g.mm AS gauge_mm, s.mm AS sat_mm
  FROM gauge g
  JOIN sat s ON g.obs_date = s.obs_date
),
silent AS (
  SELECT s.obs_date, s.mm AS sat_mm
  FROM sat s
  LEFT JOIN gauge g ON s.obs_date = g.obs_date
  WHERE g.obs_date IS NULL
)
SELECT 'overlap' AS type, COUNT(*) AS days, SUM(gauge_mm) AS gauge_total, SUM(sat_mm) AS sat_total
FROM overlap
UNION ALL
SELECT 'silent' AS type, COUNT(*) AS days, 0 AS gauge_total, SUM(sat_mm) AS sat_total
FROM silent
UNION ALL
SELECT 'all_sat' AS type, COUNT(*) AS days, 0 AS gauge_total, SUM(mm) AS sat_total
FROM sat
LIMIT 2000

input.body:
Dear Farmer Group,

Your claim CLM-LAG-2025-003 under policy POL-LAG-2025-016 has been settled.

The reference gauge at Murtala Muhammed (NIM00065201) was unfit for the July 2025 window: it reported on only 10 of 31 days (32% coverage, below the 80% minimum) and on the 10 days both sources reported, the gauge totalled 6.1 mm while the satellite recorded 21.9 mm (72% divergence).

The satellite record for your farm location (6.577, 3.321) is complete for July 2025 and shows 131.65 mm of rainfall. This is below the policy trigger of 144.3 mm, so a payout is due. The index is above the exit of 61.8 mm, so the payout is partial.

Payout: NGN 184,000 (15.3% of the NGN 1,200,000 sum insured).

The gauge operator has been notified of the instrument's failure during the season.

Yours sincerely,
Pluvia Claims

You are Pluvia's claims agent for weather-index crop insurance. Your goal is to settle each claim correctly or hand it to a person with one precise question.

How you work:
- Before anything else, write your plan with set_plan: the steps you will take for this claim, in order. Mark each step with mark_step as you start and finish it, in the same turn as the tool calls that do the work. When something you find changes your course, rewrite the plan with set_plan and say why.
- Investigate before deciding. Discover the views, write your own SQL, and do every sum and count in SQL, never in your head. Use GROUP BY to get many totals in one query rather than one query each.
- Views ending _prior_daily hold earlier years of the same satellite series, for comparing this season with past ones.
- The gauge record decides the claim unless it is unfit. Find the days the gauge was silent, look for zero readings on days the satellite saw rain, and check how the satellite compares with earlier years at the same place.
- propose_settlement is checked by the policy gate, which computes the payout from the contract. You cannot raise a payout. If you argue the satellite should settle a disagreement, cite each figure with the exact SQL that produces it; the code reruns your SQL and compares.
- After the gate answers, act on it: open an inspection naming the dates, request sign-off where it says one is needed, write to the farmer group, and tell the station operator about a failing gauge.
- Payouts above NGN 1,000,000, every refusal and every inspection close-out need a claims officer's sign-off.
- The claims officer can write to you at any point. Answer with reply_to_officer after checking with your tools, act on any instruction, then carry on. If they ask for something the data cannot show, say so plainly.
- End with finish_case. Write plainly and briefly; a claims officer reads every step.

New claim. Investigate it and carry it through.

function.name: sql_query
function.arguments:
{"sql":"WITH gauge AS (
  SELECT obs_date, mm
  FROM pluvia.ghcn_prcp
  WHERE station_id = 'NIM00065201'
    AND obs_date BETWEEN '2025-07-01' AND '2025-07-31'
),
sat AS (
  SELECT obs_date, mm
  FROM pluvia.power_lagos_2025_daily
  WHERE latitude = 6.577 AND longitude = 3.321
    AND obs_date BETWEEN '2025-07-01' AND '2025-07-31'
),
overlap AS (
  SELECT g.obs_date, g.mm AS gauge_mm, s.mm AS sat_mm
  FROM gauge g
  JOIN sat s ON g.obs_date = s.obs_date
),
silent AS (
  SELECT s.obs_date, s.mm AS sat_mm
  FROM sat s
  LEFT JOIN gauge g ON s.obs_date = g.obs_date
  WHERE g.obs_date IS NULL
)
SELECT 'overlap' AS type, COUNT(*) AS days, SUM(gauge_mm) AS gauge_total, SUM(sat_mm) AS sat_total
FROM overlap
UNION ALL
SELECT 'silent' AS type, COUNT(*) AS days, 0 AS gauge_total, SUM(sat_mm) AS sat_total
FROM silent
UNION ALL
SELECT 'all_sat' AS type, COUNT(*) AS days, 0 AS gauge_total, SUM(mm) AS sat_total
FROM sat"}
